papers.title: Strategies for breaking insecticide resistance in Spodoptera frugiperda infesting maize
papers.authors: Mandla Rajashekhar, Neeli Priyanka, Chava Asritha, Balabadra Keerthana, P. Duraimurugan
papers.abstract: The invasion of Spodoptera frugiperda (J. E. Smith, 1797) Fall armyworm (FAW) has transformed maize production into a constant battle against one of the world’s most destructive agricultural pests. Its extraordinary capacity for migration, rapid reproduction, and adaptation has enabled the pest to spread across continents and develop resistance to numerous insecticides. As chemical control becomes increasingly unreliable, sustainable solutions are urgently required. This review explores the current understanding of insecticide resistance in FAW including its causes, resistance mechanisms, and global resistance trends. It critically evaluates modern resistance management strategies such as mode-of-action-based insecticide rotation, insecticide mixtures, biological control agents, botanical pesticides, resistant maize genotypes, refugia and precision agriculture technologies. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and smart pest monitoring systems are revolutionizing resistance management through real-time surveillance and predictive decision-making. papers.title: Effects of emerald ash borer specific gene silencing using RNA interference on soil communities
papers.authors: Faith Boa
papers.abstract: The emerald ash borer (EAB) (Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire) is an invasive wood- boring beetle from Asia that primarily feeds on ash trees (Fraxinus spp.). Since its invasion of North America, EAB threatens the functional extinction of ash with damages and management costs projected to reach $900 million by 2054. Current management strategies have been insufficient to prevent EAB’s spread, highlighting the need to advance innovative approaches like RNAi, which has demonstrated efficacy against EAB in laboratory and greenhouse trials. Double-stranded RNA targeting heat shock 70-kDa protein (hsp) induces EAB mortality, systematically disperses and persists in planta, and causes no phenotypic effects for several ash-associated insects. We evaluated the environmental and nontarget effects of dsHSP, focusing on soil communities. In laboratory soil incubation assays, dsHSP was recovered up to 8 h post-treatment. Exposure of the collembolan Folsomia candida to dsHSP-treated soil had no effects on adult survival or body length, but increased reproduction. papers.title: Early detection of pine shoot beetle infestations using UAV multispectral data: The YOLOv11n-SAGE framework
papers.authors: Mingbo Chen, Lihui Zhong, Shiting Han, ZE Sang-zi, Tianqi Zhu
papers.abstract: Pine ecosystems across southwestern China face their greatest threat from the pine shoot beetle (PSB, Tomicus spp.), a highly devastating forest pest. The ability to suppress pest populations depends largely on how accurately and quickly early-stage infested pine trees are detected and removed. However, due to the inconspicuous visual features of early infestations, current deep learning-based approaches to rapid detection have focused primarily on the late stage of infestation. To address this challenge, our study proposes YOLOv11n-SAGE, an improved framework tailored for the early-stage of PSB infestations using UAV multispectral imagery. Built upon the YOLOv11n architecture, the developed model adopts a halfway fusion strategy to integrate RGB and Near-Infrared (NIR) bands. Furthermore, it incorporates a specialized P2 detection head, the Early-Stage Aware Loss (ESAL) function, and a Vegetation Index Prior Guided Progressive Spectral Fusion (VIPG-PSF) module to specifically enhance network sensitivity to small objects and subtle visual symptoms. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: Plant leaf diseases threaten agricultural productivity and motivate accurate automated monitoring. This study presents LARU-Net, a unified architecture for binary cucumber lesion segmentation (lesion versus background) with an auxiliary continuous severity-regression output on a bounded 0–4 scale. The network integrates a Disease Feature Enhancement Autoencoder, Residual Multi-Scale Encoder, transformer bottleneck, Attention-Guided Decoder, and Boundary Refinement Module. On the declared held-out test partition (1,080 images), the archived full-model results were Dice 0.9230, IoU 0.8660, Boundary F1 0.9350, and precision 0.9460; the previously emphasized Dice value of 0.9456 is a validation value and is now identified as such. Severity estimates yielded an overall MAE of 0.29, RMSE of 0.37, and R 2 of 0.90. These values are single-run point estimates from one greenhouse image collection. Plant/session identifiers, complete acquisition and annotation provenance, repeated-run logs, and an external dataset were not preserved in the supplied study archive; therefore, the results support in-domain evaluation but not broad cross-greenhouse or cross-season generalization. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.authors: Tianqi Guo, Zhongdian Zhang, Liu R, Xiaofei Wu, Xinmei Liu
papers.abstract: Abstract. As a native perennial tree, Pinus tabuliformis L. (PT) has been widely planted on the Chinese Loess Plateau for ecological restoration. However, climate change impacts on water resources will poses a new challenge for sustainability of restored ecosystems. To clarify the plantations carbon sequestration and water consumption, as well as their underlying physiological mechanisms, this study coupled the integrated BBGC-Sperry model with CMIP6 meteorological data under SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585. Daily transpiration, soil water content, and leaf water potential, along with multi-site total growing-season transpiration and aboveground biomass data, were used to validate the BBGC-Sperry model. The validated model simulated the dynamics of NPP, actual evapotranspiration (ET) and annual average percentage loss of whole-plant hydraulic conductivity (APLK) for PT plantations at 130 meteorological stations on the Loess Plateau. We integrated a “carbon-water-hydraulic risk index” (CWHRI) based on NPP, ET, and drought-induced mortality risk probability (DMRP) to assess ecosystem sustainability. papers.title: When more information is not enough: AI-enabled advisory and coordinated farming decisions under uncertainty among smallholder farmers in the Mekong Delta
papers.authors: Dinh Duc Truong, Nguyen Dieu Hang, Duong Duc Tam, Duong Thi Van Anh
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of digitally mediated and increasingly AI-enabled agricultural advisory systems, more information does not necessarily lead to more coordinated farming decisions under uncertainty. This study reconceptualizes AI-enabled advisory as a coordination-support mechanism and examines how it is associated with coordinated decision-making through three behavioural capacities: understanding system interactions, operational coordination capability, and adaptive complexity management. Using a survey dataset of 386 smallholder rice farmers from An Giang, Tra Vinh, and Ca Mau provinces in Vietnam's Mekong Delta, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that AI-enabled advisory is positively associated with all three behavioural capacities, while adaptive complexity management has the strongest association with coordinated decision-making capability (β = 0.33, p < 0.001). It also represents the strongest indirect pathway between AI-enabled advisory and coordinated decision-making (β = 0.135, p < 0.001). papers.abstract: Background: This research presents a critical analysis of mycotoxins produced by fungi, particularly the Fusarium genus, which is prevalent in cereal-producing regions. Given the global impact of mycotoxins on food safety and animal health, this study addresses an urgent issue in agricultural science. It highlights the various environmental, physical, and biological factors influencing mycotoxin production, providing valuable insights for developing effective management strategies. The study also discusses the health risks associated with specific mycotoxins, such as zearalenone and fumonisins, which have been linked to serious health issues in both animals and humans. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for ongoing prevention and control programs to mitigate mycotoxin contamination in the food chain. By exploring analytical challenges and proposing future directions for research and policy, this work contributes significantly to the understanding of mycotoxin dynamics in agricultural systems. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: A K M Kanak Pervez, Md Mahedi, Ashfaq Ahmad Shah, Shabrin Jahan Shaili, Md Nurnobi
papers.abstract: Abstract The global imperative to transition towards sustainable agricultural systems is particularly acute in vulnerable, resource-scarce regions such as the Barind Tract of Bangladesh, an area characterized by a semi-arid climate, soil infertility, and acute water scarcity. Understanding the drivers and barriers to adoption is critical, with the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) framework serving as a vital analytical tool. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of farmers' KAP towards sustainable agriculture and examines the socio-economic and institutional factors that influence them. Data were collected through structured, face-to-face interviews with 273 smallholder farmers, selected via a multi-stage random sampling technique across the Rajshahi district. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression models. The findings reveal a critical paradox: while farmers possess moderate to high levels of knowledge (Mean = 19.27) and overwhelmingly favorable attitudes (Mean = 56.34) regarding the benefits of sustainable practices, their actual adoption remains only moderate (Mean = 16.16), exposing a significant knowledge-practice gap. papers.authors: Bashiri Iddy Muzzo
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Beef cattle grazing systems in the western United States often depend on grass monocultures that decline in nutritional quality during summer. As pasture quality decreases, cattle have fewer opportunities for selective foraging, grazing efficiency declines, and producers face increased supplementation costs to maintain animal performance, welfare, and effective pasture use. This dissertation examined whether interventions that provide phytochemicals either as a supplement or through the establishment of taxonomically diverse “hot spots” in otherwise monotonous landscapes could improve cow-calf pair performance and enhance the sustainability of agroecosystems. The study tested two strategies with free-grazing cow–calf pairs: supplementation with tannin extract and establishing of small patches, or “islands,” of diverse, phytochemically rich forage species within bromegrass pastures. Using combined GPS–tri-axial accelerometer collars, pedometers, and machine-learning methods, the study identified cattle behavioral responses to these feeding strategies with high accuracy. papers.abstract: Climate change is increasingly threatening the sustainability and productivity of horticultural fruit production, particularly in mountainous countries such as Nepal, where diverse agro-ecological regional conditions and smallholder farming systems are highly sensitive to climatic variability.This review investigated the impacts of climate change on major horticultural fruit crops in Nepal, with particular emphasis on apple (Malus domestica), citrus (Citrus spp.), mango (Mangifera indica), and kiwifruit (Actinidia deliciosa).The study synthesizes recent scientific evidence about the effects of rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, drought, reduced winter chilling, and other extreme weather events on fruit phenology, flowering, fruit set, yield, quality, and post-harvest performance.The review also investigates emerging changes in pest and disease incidence and their implications for orchard productivity and smallholder livelihoods across diverse agro-ecological zones of Nepal.Furthermore, it evaluates climate-resilient adaptation and mitigation approaches, comprising stress-tolerant cultivar development, improved irrigation system and water-use efficiency, climate-smart orchard ma

papers.authors: Jacki Heraud-Farlow, Yu-Pei Chan, Sophia Davidson, Carl R. Walkley
papers.abstract: Cells must continuously distinguish cellular-derived RNA from pathogenic RNA to mount effective antiviral responses while avoiding harmful autoinflammation. Cytoplasmic RNA-sensing receptors, including RIG-I-like receptors, PKR, OAS-RNase L and ZBP1, detect RNA primarily through molecular features such as structure (double- versus single-stranded), modification state and subcellular localization rather than sequence. While these are characteristics of viral nucleic acids, mammalian genomes generate abundant self-derived double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), including from transposable elements, antisense transcription and RNA processing intermediates, which exist in the cytoplasm. This review describes our current understanding of how cells achieve self-tolerance through the active regulation of endogenous RNA. These mechanisms comprise epigenetic silencing of repetitive elements, RNA modifications (such as A-to-I editing and m6A), precise splicing, regulated nuclear export and decay, circRNA buffering, protein shielding and dedicated RNA degradation pathways. papers.authors: Romina De Angelis, Mirriam Matita, Shiphar Mulumba, Carolyne Phiri, Frank Tchuwa

papers.abstract: Introduction Farmer Research Networks (FRNs) are collaborative platforms that bring together diverse stakeholders to co-create knowledge and support agroecological innovation. While FRNs are increasingly recognised for enabling farmers to embrace sustainable practices and strengthen resilience, limited evidence exists on how they influence farmer behaviour and contribute to agroecological systems change. Methods This study draws on a single round of qualitative fieldwork conducted in 2024 with nine FRNs that had been operating since 2015 in Kenya, Malawi, and Uganda, comprising 99 interviews and focus group discussions with 182 farmers, researchers and extension or NGO staff, to examine how engagement in these FRNs shapes farmers’ attitudes, perceptions, intentions, and practices. The Theory of Planned Behaviour, the Model of Justified Behaviour, and the FAO’s 10 elements of agroecology were used as analytical lenses. papers.authors: Timothy P Lampasona, Cesar Rodriguez‐Saona, Anne L. Nielsen
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Plum curculio, Conotrachelus nenuphar (Herbst), is a native fruit pest. Adults emerge from overwintering sites in wooded areas and disperse into crop fields in the spring. However, their movement patterns within fields after this initial dispersal remain poorly understood. In this study, we used protein markers to investigate the in‐field dispersal of C. nenuphar adults in peach ( Prunus persica L.) and highbush blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum L.) fields. Chicken egg albumin (egg whites) was applied along field borders and bovine casein (cow's milk) within field interiors. Adults were collected daily using beat sampling, and enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA) were used to detect egg and/or milk proteins on individual insects. This approach provided a form of behavioural forensics, allowing us to trace each insect's movement within the field. Results indicated a strong edge effect in both crops, with 64.3% and 78.0% of adults collected along the border in blueberry and peach, respectively. papers.title: Effects of moss restoration on topsoil water dynamics in a temperate vineyard
papers.authors: Silvana Oldenburg, Martin Nebel, Steffen Seitz, Corinna Gall
papers.abstract: Abstract. Climate change is intensifying pressure on vineyard soil and water management, particularly under-vine, where vegetation is commonly suppressed to minimize competition with grapevines. Bryophytes represent a promising but little-tested alternative to bare soil or cover crops. We evaluated moss restoration as an under-vine ground cover in a temperate, rainfed vineyard in southwestern Germany, comparing it with bare soil and cover crop (grass) over a 22-month field experiment. Continuous topsoil moisture measurements using time-domain transmission sensors were used to analyse the initial response time (the time between the onset of precipitation and the first increase in topsoil moisture) and the peak response time (the time between the onset of precipitation and the maximum topsoil moisture). We additionally quantified mean topsoil moisture and drying rates and monitored treatment development during and after maintenance. Moss restoration did not significantly delay topsoil moisture response times following precipitation compared to grass or bare soil. papers.abstract: Abstract Acid-extractable concentrations of Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, As, Cd and Pb were measured by ICP-MS in 80 composite topsoil samples collected from five agricultural sites in the West Bank, Palestine, near wastewater sources or a landfill. Pollution indices calculated relative to continental-crust values differed among sites but are conditional on the partial extraction and selected background. papers.title: Oribatid mites in sustainable agriculture: Evidence for organic-matter processing, nutrient cycling and crop responses: A review
papers.authors: AT Patel, KM Patel, TR Darji
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
papers.abstract: Modern crop production often depends on external nutrient inputs, yet soil health cannot be sustained by fertilizer use alone. Soil organisms contribute to the breakdown of residues, nutrient turnover and the physical and biological functioning of soil. Oribatid mites (Acari: Oribatida) are among these organisms and are associated with litter processing, microbial interactions and indicators of soil condition. The proposed practice termed “oriculture” explores whether selected litter-feeding oribatid mites can be managed to support organic-residue transformation. Published studies report changes in the nutrient composition of mite-processed litter and, in some experimental systems, improved plant growth. These outcomes should be interpreted in relation to the mite species, substrate and experimental conditions. Oribatid communities are also shaped by soil moisture, temperature, organic matter and management. This review evaluates evidence on their ecological functions, possible agricultural applications, culture methods, environmental responses and research needs. papers.title: Influence of Sustainable Agricultural Practices on Microbial Aspects of Soil
papers.authors: Dušan Adamov, Milica Vranešević, Dragana Stamenov, Simonida Đurić
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil is a non-renewable natural resource essential for supporting plants, animals, and microorganisms. The intensification of conventional agriculture has substantially affected soil health, including its microbial component. This review evaluates how sustainable agricultural practices, including crop rotation, intercropping, cover cropping, organic amendments, and agroforestry, influence microbial aspects of soil health, with particular emphasis on microbial biomass, diversity, community composition, and functions related to nutrient cycling. Peer-reviewed studies published up to 2025 were identified through Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar using combinations of terms describing individual agricultural practices and microbial soil health parameters. The reviewed evidence indicates that crop diversification can enhance microbial biomass and modify microbial community composition through changes in soil properties, nutrient cycling, root exudation, and organic inputs, although responses vary among cropping systems and environmental conditions. This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based agents are emerging as a transformative paradigm for agriculture, enabling autonomous perception, reasoning, decision-making, and coordinated action across complex data and operational environments. These systems could improve productivity, resilience, resource efficiency, and food security, while raising challenges related to robustness, interoperability, data governance, trust, equity, and regulation. papers.authors: Preeti Singh, Kumar, Preeti Bagri, Kanisht Batra, Deepika Lather
papers.source: OpenAlex / Naunyn-Schmiedeberg s Archives of Pharmacology
papers.abstract: Abstract Quinalphos (QNP), an organophosphate insecticide, is known to induce genotoxic and cytotoxic effects in non-target organisms. This study evaluated the impact of subacute QNP exposure on chromosomal stability, DNA integrity, and apoptosis-related gene expression in bone marrow cells of male Swiss albino mice, and assessed the genoprotective potential of piperine (PIP), a bioactive compound from Piper nigrum. Mice were allocated into six groups: control (2% gum acacia), QNP I (0.375 mg/kg b.w.), QNP II (0.75 mg/kg b.w.), PIP alone (10 mg/kg b.w.), QNP I + PIP, and QNP II + PIP. All treatments were administered orally for 28 days. Genotoxicity was evaluated using micronucleus, chromosomal aberration, and alkaline comet assays. QNP caused a significant, dose-dependent increase in micronucleated erythrocytes, chromosomal aberrations, and DNA strand breaks, along with suppression of erythropoiesis. It also upregulated pro-apoptotic Bax and downregulated anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 mRNA expression, indicating activation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. papers.abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes of the Anopheles , Aedes , and Culex genera serve as vectors for significant human and animal diseases. The increasing prevalence of insecticide resistance, primarily mediated by detoxification enzymes, highlights the urgent need for innovative biocontrol strategies. This study assessed the larvicidal activity of secondary metabolites produced by Klebsiella pneumoniae PX652414 and Proteus mirabilis PZ337687, as well as their impact on esterase and glutathione-S-transferase (GST) enzyme activities in three major mosquito species: An. gambiae s.l., Ae. aegypti , and Cx. quinquefasciatus .
